{{Short description|German mathematician (1823–1913)}}

'''Theodor Spieker''' (8 August 1823 – 9 April 1913) was a German mathematician, a teacher at a [[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] in [[Potsdam]].<ref>{{citation|title=Die Schwerpunkte des Dreiecks|first=Franz|last=Embacher|journal=Mathematische Semesterberichte|year=2008|volume=55|issue=2|pages=131–148|doi=10.1007/s00591-008-0040-8|s2cid=122490596|url=http://homepage.univie.ac.at/franz.embacher/MatheDidaktik/Schwerpunkte.pdf}}.</ref>

Spieker's geometry textbook {{lang|de|Lehrbuch der ebenen Geometrie mit Übungs-Aufgaben für höhere Lehranstalten}} (Verlag von August Stein, Potsdam, 1862)<ref>[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/162236270 Worldcat entry] for ''Lehrbuch der ebenen Geometrie'', accessed 2012-05-05.</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=kHALAAAAYAAJ ''Lehrbuch der ebenen Geometrie mit Übungs-Aufgaben für höhere Lehranstalten''] (1898 ed.) on Google Books, accessed 2012-05-05.</ref> was republished in many editions. A copy of this textbook was given to [[Albert Einstein]] by his tutor when Einstein was twelve, and quickly led Einstein to become interested in higher mathematics.<ref>{{citation|title=Einstein: The Life and Times|first=Ronald W.|last=Clark|publisher=HarperCollins|year=1984|isbn=9780380011599|page=34|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6IKVA0lY6MAC&pg=PA34}}.</ref>

Spieker is the namesake of the [[Spieker circle]] of a triangle (the circle inscribed in its [[medial triangle]]) and the [[Spieker center]] (the center of the Spieker circle).
